name: China economy
summary: China's October CPI rose 0.7% and factory prices 5.7%; weak lending expected but no deflation or contagion found
state: China's consumer prices rose 0.7% in the year to October and producer prices 5.7%, the fastest in more than four years, on energy and raw-material costs (CGTN, 9 Nov). A Caixin survey on 9 Nov expected October new yuan loans of only about 90 billion yuan, with an 800 billion yuan policy financing tool supporting broader credit. No new developer default wave or financial contagion was found as of 12 Nov, so Normal holds.
for_you: Rising Chinese factory prices can feed into the cost of imported goods. Exporters to China are exposed to weak household credit demand there.
rubric_hit: Normal: no deflation (CPI +0.7%), Q3 growth near target, no developer default wave or contagion

sources.title: CGTN — China's October CPI up 0.7%, PPI rises 5.7%
Caixin Global — China policy tool seen lifting October social financing

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
